# Code pipeline hooks

Read a code pipeline run's inputs, variables and step results, set its variables, and write to its log, from a hook.

**Library:** [Code pipeline hooks](index.md#code-pipeline-hooks), for code-pipeline hooks. More in [Hooks: what happens next](../../../concepts/code-pipelines.md#hooks-what-happens-next).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`PipelineGetInput`](#pipelinegetinput) | Gets one of the inputs a code pipeline run was started with. |
| [`PipelineGetStepFailure`](#pipelinegetstepfailure) | Gets why one step of a code pipeline run failed. |
| [`PipelineGetStepOutput`](#pipelinegetstepoutput) | Gets the result of one step of a code pipeline run: its agent's final reply. |
| [`PipelineGetVariable`](#pipelinegetvariable) | Gets the value of one of a code pipeline run's variables. |
| [`PipelineLog`](#pipelinelog) | Writes a message to Maitento's own service log, tagged with the run's id. |
| [`PipelineSetVariable`](#pipelinesetvariable) | Sets one of a code pipeline run's variables, creating it if it isn't there. |

### PipelineGetInput

Gets one of the inputs a code pipeline run was started with.

```c
string PipelineGetInput(guid processId, string name)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The hook's own code pipeline run: the `processId` every hook function receives as its first parameter. Pass that on; any other run's id is refused, so a hook can only use its own run. |
| `name` | `string` | The input's name, such as `request`. |

**Returns** `string`: The input's value, or empty text when the run has no input of that name.

Inputs are the values given when the run starts, such as `request`, and they don't change during it; for values set while it runs, use [`PipelineGetVariable`](#pipelinegetvariable). A prompt can only suggest an input to an agent, as `%%input:name%%`, but a hook can act on it, which makes an input the place for a setting a hook must enforce. Names match exactly, including case. An input the run wasn't given gives empty text. Another run's id fails, because a hook can only read its own run.

### PipelineGetStepFailure

Gets why one step of a code pipeline run failed.

```c
string PipelineGetStepFailure(guid processId, string phaseName, string stepName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The hook's own code pipeline run: the `processId` every hook function receives as its first parameter. Pass that on; any other run's id is refused, so a hook can only use its own run. |
| `phaseName` | `string` | The phase's name, such as `test`. |
| `stepName` | `string` | The step's name within the phase, such as `run-tests`. |

**Returns** `string`: Why the step failed, or empty text when it didn't.

Useful in an `onFailHook`, to decide whether to retry or carry on. The step is found as [`PipelineGetStepOutput`](#pipelinegetstepoutput) finds it. A step that didn't fail gives empty text, as do names that match nothing. Another run's id fails, because a hook can only read its own run. When a failed step is resumed and runs again, its failure is cleared.

### PipelineGetStepOutput

Gets the result of one step of a code pipeline run: its agent's final reply.

```c
string PipelineGetStepOutput(guid processId, string phaseName, string stepName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The hook's own code pipeline run: the `processId` every hook function receives as its first parameter. Pass that on; any other run's id is refused, so a hook can only use its own run. |
| `phaseName` | `string` | The phase's name, such as `test`. |
| `stepName` | `string` | The step's name within the phase, such as `run-tests`. |

**Returns** `string`: The step's result, or empty text when it has none.

For a step with `outputJsonSchema`, the result is the JSON that matches the schema. The step is found by its phase's name and its own: the names in the pipeline definition, or those of a phase a hook added, such as `fix-1`. For a step that failed, the result can be its error text, so check [`PipelineGetStepFailure`](#pipelinegetstepfailure) too. A step that hasn't run gives empty text, as do names that match nothing. Another run's id fails, because a hook can only read its own run.

### PipelineGetVariable

Gets the value of one of a code pipeline run's variables.

```c
string PipelineGetVariable(guid processId, string name)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The hook's own code pipeline run: the `processId` every hook function receives as its first parameter. Pass that on; any other run's id is refused, so a hook can only use its own run. |
| `name` | `string` | The variable's name, such as `testReport`. |

**Returns** `string`: The variable's value, or empty text when it isn't set.

Variables are the run's working values: a step's `outputVariableName` stores the step's reply in one, [`PipelineSetVariable`](#pipelinesetvariable) sets one, and a step's prompt reads one as `%%name%%`. They change as the run goes on; the values the run was started with are its inputs, which [`PipelineGetInput`](#pipelinegetinput) reads. Names match exactly, including case. A variable that isn't set gives empty text. Another run's id fails, because a hook can only read its own run.

### PipelineLog

Writes a message to Maitento's own service log, tagged with the run's id.

```c
void PipelineLog(guid processId, string message)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The hook's own code pipeline run: the `processId` every hook function receives as its first parameter. Pass that on; any other run's id is refused, so a hook can only use its own run. |
| `message` | `string` | The text to log. |

The message doesn't appear on the run, in the portal or through the API: the log is for Maitento's operators. To record something that you, or a later step, can read, set a variable with [`PipelineSetVariable`](#pipelinesetvariable).

### PipelineSetVariable

Sets one of a code pipeline run's variables, creating it if it isn't there.

```c
void PipelineSetVariable(guid processId, string name, string value)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `processId` | `guid` | The hook's own code pipeline run: the `processId` every hook function receives as its first parameter. Pass that on; any other run's id is refused, so a hook can only use its own run. |
| `name` | `string` | The variable's name, such as `testsPassed`. |
| `value` | `string` | Its new value, as text. |

[`PipelineGetVariable`](#pipelinegetvariable) sees the new value at once, and steps that start after the hook read it as `%%name%%` in their prompts. Names that start with `__` are Maitento's own, and fail with `Variable name '<name>' is reserved (__ prefix is for internal use)`. Fails with `A hook can only use its own run: pass the processId the hook was given` for another run's id. When two hooks set variables of the same run at the same moment, one of the changes can be lost.
